theme: ज्ञान का प्रकाश और जीवन का केंद्र / The light of knowledge and the center of life
context: Krishna now tells Arjuna that the teaching He is about to give is complete and integrative. This is not a pile of doctrines but a realization that resolves the central question of life: what is the deepest truth, and how does one live in relation to it?
contextHindi: कृष्ण अब अर्जुन को बताते हैं कि वे जो ज्ञान दे रहे हैं, वह पूर्ण और समग्र है। यह कोई कागज़ी विचार नहीं है; यह वह सच्चाई है जो जीवन के केंद्र को समझाती है कि सबसे गहरा सत्य क्या है और उससे जुड़ते हुए मन कैसे जीता है।
sanskritDevanagari:
ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः |
यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ||७-२||
transliteration:
jñānaṃ te.ahaṃ savijñānamidaṃ vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ .
yajjñātvā neha bhūyo.anyajjñātavyamavaśiṣyate ||7-2||

wordByWord.meaning: jñānaṃ — true understanding, the deepest knowing of reality.
savijñānam — together with realization; not just theory, but experiential understanding.
aśeṣataḥ — in full, completely, without remainder.
yajjñātvā — after knowing which; once this is understood, the central question is answered.
avaśiṣyate — remains; nothing further remains to be known in the same essential way.

spokenHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं, “मैं तुम्हें यह ज्ञान विज्ञान सहित पूरी तरह बताऊँगा। इसे जान लेने पर यहाँ फिर कुछ और जानना बाकी नहीं रहेगा।” ‘ज्ञानम्’ का अर्थ है ज्ञान या समझ। ‘सविज्ञानम्’ का अर्थ है विज्ञान सहित; इस श्लोक के संदर्भ में, ज्ञान के साथ उसकी अनुभूति भी। ‘अशेषतः’ का अर्थ है पूरा, बिना कुछ छोड़े। ‘यज्ज्ञात्वा’ का अर्थ है, जिसे जान लेने पर। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि इस ज्ञान को जान लेने के बाद यहाँ कुछ और जानना बाकी नहीं रहता। श्लोक इतना ही कहता है; यह यहाँ आत्मा और परमात्मा के संबंध को इस ज्ञान का विषय बताकर नहीं समझाता। आगे कृष्ण इस ज्ञान को विस्तार से बताएँगे। अभी वे अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि वह उनकी बात सुने और समझे कि वे किस ज्ञान को पूरी तरह बताने वाले हैं।
clearEnglish: Krishna is teaching that the highest knowledge is not an endless accumulation of facts; it is the direct seeing of the essential truth. 'jñānaṃ' is understanding in its deepest sense, and 'savijñānam' adds the element of experiential realization—knowing not only what is true but also how it lives in consciousness. The verse says that this knowledge is given in full, 'aśeṣataḥ.' Knowing it, 'neha bhūyo 'nyaj jñātavyam avaśiṣyate'—nothing further remains to be known here. This does not mean that the path ends in a closed encyclopedia of doctrine; it means that the central issue is resolved. A seeker has found the organizing center of reality. TEXT: Krishna says He will explain knowledge together with realization in full, and that after knowing it nothing further remains to be known here. The verse does not explicitly say that this knowledge brings liberation. INFERENCE: a mature spiritual life is less about collecting beliefs than about being oriented by a stable, personal, and truthful understanding of the Divine.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse says Krishna will explain this knowledge together with realization in full; it adds that, having known it, nothing further remains to be known here. It does not itself state that this knowledge grants liberation.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The practical inference is that spiritual maturity is not a larger collection of concepts but a more settled understanding that changes perception, judgment, and action. Wisdom becomes a center, not a library.

practicalApplication.label: One question, one truth
practicalApplication.text: At the end of the day, ask: 'What did I understand today that actually changed how I responded to my own mind, my duties, or my relationships?'

reflectionQuestion: What in your life would change if you treated one deep truth as a living center, not merely a concept to remember?
reflectionQuestionHindi: यदि आप एक गहरी सच्चाई को केवल याद रखने वाली बात नहीं, बल्कि जीवन का केंद्र मानें, तो आपके जीवन में क्या बदलता?
